newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Surgeon says Yeltsin to be able to work normally.
newsitem.headline: Surgeon says Yeltsin to be able to work normally.

text.p: Doctors involved in President Boris Yeltsin's bypass operation declared it a complete success on Tuesday and said he would be able to resume normal work.
"I find it a great pleasure to confirm that the operation was a complete success," veteran U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, an observer at Yeltsin's operation, said.

"President Yeltsin will be able to return to his office and carry out his duties in normal fashion," he told a news conference at the Cardiology Research Centre where the surgery took place, adding that Yeltsin was receiving expert care.
Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin, who led the operating team, said there had been no surprises.
"Nothing extraordinary has emerged. All indications are that the heart muscle is getting enough blood to function normally," said Akchurin, looking exhausted after seven hours of surgery.
"Now the very important stage of post-operative treatment is starting."
The operation, which began at 7 a.m. (0400 GMT) and ended at 2 p.m. (1100 GMT), was intended to bypass clogged cardiac arteries and allow the 65-year-old president to resume his normal routine.
Akchurin said his team had made more than the expected three or four bypasses but declined to give a precise figure, saying it was up to Yeltsin to decide whether to make it public.
"The formal number of bypasses is not that important."

Doctors have said the post-operative stage is a crucial part of Yeltsin's treatment and specialists advising the Russian doctors on the operation include two experienced German specialists in this sphere.
Akchurin said Yeltsin would decide himself when to resume his presidential responsibilities, which he transferred to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin minutes before surgery.

"He will decide himself, in all probability it will be tomorrow or the day after -- touch wood," he said, adding that Yeltsin was still under anaesthesia and his lungs were being ventilated artificially.
"This is normal and is usually done to prevent post-surgery complications," he said. Yeltsin's heart was stopped for 68 minutes during the operation, Akchurin said.
